crime: Every morning at free time, a girl skipped flat stones across the lake, counting each bounce aloud, and {WITCH_NAME} stood beside her to keep her company.

As a child, carrying her baby sister, she had told her mother what she kept thinking: what if I opened my arms? Her mother lifted the baby out of them, and never let her hold her again. Ever since, whenever a cruel thought came, she used her Magic to draw it out of her head and kept the stone in her pocket, proof of what she was.

One morning at the lake, a thought came: push her under. She drew it from her temple, and it lay in her palm, small and grey. The girl took it, held it a moment, and said, "Oh. Everyone thinks that." Then she skipped it across the water. "Seven, eight, nine." It sank. {WITCH_NAME} waded in after it and felt along the bottom, but she never found it.

The prisoners found the girl drowned in the lake, a flat stone clenched in her fist. It looked as if she had waded out gathering skipping stones and slipped. Then one prisoner pried the fist open and held the stone, and thought, as plainly as her own memory: I held her under until she went still.

The thought was {WITCH_NAME}'s, and so was the deed, done during free time. Afterward she drew the thought out as a stone, pressed it into the girl's cold hand, and closed the fingers over it for whoever would open them.
fields.epitaph: "Everyone thinks that," the girl had said, and she was right. Only the deed was ever hers.
execution: On the execution stand in the trial court, she is strapped beneath a stone hopper, arms spread wide, palms open. The hopper tips, and small grey stones pour steadily onto her chest, piling higher and higher. They fill her open palms. The stones keep coming until there is only a grey mound, and beneath it she lies still.

magic.name: Thought Stones
magic.text: She draws her thoughts out as small stones; whoever holds one thinks it exactly as she does.
